response.answer: Paulo Rogerio Gonzalez Alonso is a leading researcher in agent architecture evaluation, known for developing AgentArcEval, a method for assessing foundation model-based agents. His work combines practical insights with systematic literature reviews. He is highly regarded in the field for his contributions.

results.title: AgentArcEval: An Architecture Evaluation Method for Foundation Model based Agents
results.content: Evaluating the architecture of agents is particularly important, as agents are complex compound AI systems that integrate FMs with a variety of out-of-model components, including context engines, prompt optimisers, reasoning and planning, workflow execution, memory, external knowledge bases and tools, guardrails, etc. To support the agent architecture evaluation using AgentArcEval, we present a catalogue of agent-specific general scenarios, providing a structured guide for generating concrete scenarios to design and evaluate agent architecture. To develop the AgentArcEval method and the corresponding catalogue of agent-specific general scenarios, we undertook a structured approach that combined insights from our hands-on project experience with a systematic literature review (SLR) of existing architecture evaluation papers. By combining practical insights from real-world projects with an SLR of existing methods, we were able to design the AgentArcEval method and the general scenario catalogue to address both theoretical gaps and operational considerations of agent architecture evaluations.

results.title: AI Agents as Humans // Social experiments simulations | by noailabs | Medium
results.content: March 13, 2025 - Generative Agent Architecture: The authors developed a generative agent architecture that uses two-hour qualitative interviews to simulate individuals’ attitudes and behaviors. These agents are designed to replicate real individuals’ responses to surveys and experiments, achieving high accuracy in predicting their attitudes, personality traits, and behaviors. Evaluation Metrics: The agents were evaluated using canonical social science measures, including the General Social Survey (GSS), the Big Five Personality Inventory, and behavioral economic games.
